subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Grid-Scale Battery Storage: Saving the Sun for Night
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Grid-Scale Battery Storage: Saving the Sun for Night.

hook.text: The sun doesn't shine at night. Wind doesn't blow on demand. Grid-scale batteries store renewable energy for when it's needed.

buildup.text: Tesla's Hornsdale battery stores 194 megawatt-hours. It responds to grid needs in milliseconds — faster than any gas plant.

discovery.text: Lithium-ion dominates, but iron-air batteries store energy at one-tenth the cost. They're heavier but ideal for grid storage.

twist.text: Pumped hydro is 95% of grid storage worldwide. Water is pumped uphill when cheap and released through turbines when needed.

climax.text: California's grid regularly curtails solar — there's more than it can use. Storage is the bottleneck, not generation.

punchline.text: Generate when the sun shines. Store it. Use it at midnight.

quiz.question: What technology accounts for 95% of grid-scale energy storage worldwide?
options: Lithium-ion battery farms installed at solar and wind generation sites
Pumped hydro storage that moves water uphill and releases it through turbines
Compressed air stored in underground caverns and released to spin generators
